doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Blue Note, The Connection and Tony Williams
title: Control at Blue Note over music, titles and musicians
summary: McLean cared only about choosing musicians and music; he named New Soil but hated Swing, Swing, Swing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: When you got to Blue Note – just looking at the titles of the things – did you have control over the images, over the titling, over the notes, over the repertoire? Did they give you control of all those things?

Those are things that I would have thought of if I was an ordinary guy like Donald Byrd that didn’t have the problems that I had. I didn’t even care about that. I had control over the music. That’s what I really cared about, that I had choice of the musicians. I could pick the musicians that I wanted, and then I could play the music that I wanted. All they wanted to do was hear it.
Like I didn’t name Swing, Swing, Swing, and I hated that title when they told me they were going to name it that.
I named that. That was like a new place that I was coming to, to plant seeds. That was the whole idea of that. Left Prestige, and I was now on new soil.
